subject: design-technology

moments.title: Wedgwood opens his factory
moments.body: Wedgwood develops standardised ceramic bodies and division of labour for pottery production.
moments.takeaway: Pottery was an early industrial design test bed.

moments.title: Queen's Ware
moments.body: Queen Charlotte allows Wedgwood to call his cream-coloured earthenware 'Queen's Ware', an early endorsement deal.
moments.takeaway: Brand association with royalty is older than modern marketing.

moments.title: Anti-slavery medallion
moments.body: Wedgwood produces 'Am I Not a Man and a Brother?' medallions, free of charge, for the abolitionist campaign.
moments.takeaway: Industrial design served political campaigns as well as profit.

now.title: Wedgwood now
now.body: The Wedgwood company has changed ownership repeatedly. The British anti-slavery medallion is a key object in design-history teaching.
now.open_questions: What does ethically-aligned mass production look like today?

reflection: Wedgwood was a designer, factory owner and political activist at once.
